mintAuthority.summary: HLUSD issuance is controlled by HeLa's on-chain governance roles: MintProposer initiates mint requests, MintVoter approval satisfies the configured quorum, and Admin configures role/quorum parameters.

controls.label: HeLa MintProposer/MintVoter quorum
controls.evidence: HeLa governance docs define HLUSD minting as a chain-runtime quorum action: MintProposer addresses propose mints to whitelisted users and MintVoter addresses approve until mintQuorum is reached; proposals and votes execute inside the HeLa runtime (not an EVM contract). The HeLa mainnet EVM gateway (mainnet-rpc.helachain.com, chain id 8668) is live, but the native role state is exposed only through the HeLa runtime API/CLI (hela managest), so individual role-holder addresses remain unenumerated through standard JSON-RPC.

controls.label: HeLa Admin role
controls.evidence: HeLa governance docs state the Admin role proposes and votes on all other roles and configures mintQuorum, burnQuorum, whitelistQuorum, blacklistQuorum, and configQuorum within the HeLa runtime's on-chain proposal system; the initial Chain Initiator assignment is single-use and afterwards all role management flows through propose-vote governance.

controls.label: HeLa runtime upgrade authority (unresolved)
controls.evidence: 2026-08-08 re-check: HeLa stablecoin-governance docs still define only mint/burn/whitelist/blacklist/config/setroles actions and publish neither a runtime bytecode-upgrade executor nor its threshold or delay. Architecture documentation confirms that execution layers can be upgraded independently, while tokenomics only says $HELA holders may participate in protocol upgrades. The live public gateway returned chain id 8668 and block 660832, but standard JSON-RPC exposes no runtime role or upgrade-admin state. The authority model therefore remains issuer-undisclosed rather than guessed.

review.evidence: The documented model is clear but the live controller inventory is not: MintProposer/MintVoter may propose and approve arbitrary mint amounts to whitelisted users once mintQuorum is reached, and Admin governs the role/quorum configuration. No numeric supply cap is documented, so economic cap semantics remain unbounded; as a runtime-governed native asset, reserve reconciliation is not applicable. On 2026-08-08 the official EVM gateway was live at chain id 8668 and block 660832, but it exposes neither the runtime-native role roster/current quorum values nor the runtime code-upgrade authority. Current governance, architecture, endpoint, tokenomics, whitepaper, explorer, and public repository review still identify no upgrade executor, threshold, or timelock. The review is therefore explicitly unresolved rather than scoreable. Re-checked 2026-08-09 with new source-level evidence: the stablecoin governance module is public in HelaNetwork/helanetwork-sdk (runtime-sdk/src/modules/accounts/mod.rs), where mint executes inside the vote handler once yes-votes from MintVoter holders reach ceil(voter_total * quorum / 100), quorum defaults to 100 when never configured, and the mint routine carries no supply-cap check, so caps remain unbounded in code. A direct MintST path exists with no caller-role check, gated only by the mintst_disabled runtime parameter; the public EVM-runtime genesis (helanetwork-evm-runtime/src/lib.rs) was re-read on 2026-08-09 and still sets mintst_disabled: true, burnst_disabled: true and hard-codes chain_initiator hela01qp3fu89xmt5s3trszky6k6z0e2qka9hklsj5h6jn. The live gateway re-read the same day returned eth_chainId 0x21dc (8668) and web3_clientVersion 'oasis/hela-mainnet-20251014-git4f94f25/go1.19.3'; that commit is absent from the public HelaNetwork repositories, so drift between the deployed runtime and the public source cannot be excluded. The live MintProposer/MintVoter/Admin roster and configured quorum values remain enumerable only through oasis-node runtime queries (accounts.RoleAddresses / accounts.Quorum / accounts.Parameters, per helanetwork-cli cmd/managest.go) and no public gRPC endpoint exposes them, so the review stays unresolved. Economic-posture fields reviewed 2026-08-15: role governance can approve uncapped minting, but the off-chain USDC reserve claim has no dated whole-supply reconciliation and no named prudential supervisor. Wave 2 external research reviewed 2026-08-15: HeLa, StableHodl, explorer, whitepaper, and public repository searches found no dated reserve statement or assets-to-native-supply report, so reconciliation remains unknown.

review.sourceFreeRationale: Classification based on the role-based mint governance model in HeLa documentation; the on-chain role holder addresses could not be resolved because HLUSD's native HeLa chain is not modeled in Pharos contracts.
unresolvedQuestions: What are the current MintProposer, MintVoter, and Admin holder addresses and configured quorum values on the HeLa runtime?
Which address or governance executor can upgrade the HLUSD runtime logic, and what threshold and delay govern that action?
